newsitem.title: GREECE: One-year swaps up, Greek bonds down in late trade.
newsitem.headline: One-year swaps up, Greek bonds down in late trade.

text.p: One-year forex swaps were trading higher, money market rates were stable, ecu/drachma was higher and taxable and tax-free bonds were trading lower in late Monday dealings, dealers said.
"There was interest to sell bonds by foreign investors and Greek banks. Prices of taxable and non-taxable bonds were trading lower late on Monday," a state bank bond dealer said.
Money market rates were steady and one-year swaps were trading 10 basis points higher, dealers said.
"With news about a possible delay in the realisation of EMU, all high-yield Mediterranean currencies markets were down. There was a capital outflow from these markets," a state-bank dealer said.
The central bank kept its intervention rate in overnight money unchanged at 11.90 percent.
The mark was quoted at 157.25/30 from Monday's 157.300 fix, the dollar at 265.98/08 drachmas from 266.100 and the Ecu at 304.85/90 from 305.190 drachmas.

"The ecu was trading higher at 305.30-40. There were buyers of ecus and sellers of drachmas. We believe drachma sellers could be people who liquidated their positions in the Greek bourse," a state-bank dealer said.
